rdl_0001.question: What is round as a dishpan, deep as a tub, and still the oceans couldn't fill it up?

rdl_0002.question: You are on a ship, over the side hangs a rope ladder with half meter rungs. The tide rises a half meter per hour. At the end of five hours, how much of the ladder will remain above the water assuming that nine rungs were above the water when the tide began to rise?
rdl_0002.answer: Remember the tde Nine rungs will be above the water. As the tide rises, so will the ship and the ladder

rdl_0003.question: I have many feathers to help me fly. I have a body and head, but I'm not alive. It is your strength which determines how far I go. You can hold me in your hand, but I'm never thrown. What am I?

rdl_0004.question: I'm in the book, but not on any leaf; I'm in the mouth, but not in lip or teeth; I'm in the atmosphere, but never in the air; I wait on every one, but never on a pair; I am with you wherever you may go; And every thing you do I'm sure to know; Though when you did it I should not be there, Yet when 'twas done, you'd find me in the chair. What am I ?

rdl_0005.question: I'm as small as an ant, as big as a whale. I'll approach like a breeze but can come like a gale. By some, I get hit, but all have shown fear. I'll dance to the music, though I can't hear. Of names, I have many, of names I have one. I'm as slow as a snail, but from me, you can't run. What am I ?

rdl_0006.question: What God never sees, what the king seldom sees, and what we see every day. What is it? Read my riddle .

rdl_0007.question: What can be heard and caught but never seen?

rdl_0008.question: Not born, but from a Mother's body drawn, I hang until half of me is gone. I sleep in a cave until I grow old, then valued for my hardened gold. What am I?

rdl_0009.question: Black I am and much admired, men seek me until they're tired. When they find me, they break my head, and take from me my resting bed. What am I?

rdl_0010.question: I am as light as a feather, yet no man can hold me for long. What am I ?

rdl_0011.question: I am not alive, but I grow; I don't have lungs, but I need air; I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I ?

rdl_0012.question: I was carried into a dark room and set on fire. I wept, and then my head was cut off. What am I?

rdl_0013.question: This old one runs forever but never moves at all. It has not lungs nor throat, but still a mighty roaring call. What is it?

rdl_0014.question: I pass before the sun, yet make no shadow. What am I ?

rdl_0015.question: I killed one fourth of all mankind. Who am I?

rdl_0016.question: Why are your nose and chin always at variance?
rdl_0016.answer: Because words are passing between them.

rdl_0017.question: It speaks with a hard tongue, it cannot breathe, for it has no lungs. What is it?

rdl_0018.question: Why ought a fisherman to be very wealthy?
rdl_0018.answer: Because his is all net profit.

rdl_0019.question: How high would you have to count before you would use the letter A in the English language spelling of a whole number?

rdl_0020.question: We are little creatures; all of us have different features. One of us in glass is set; one of us you'll find in jet. Another you may see in tin, and the fourth is boxed within. If the fifth you should pursue, it can never fly from you. What are we?

rdl_0021.question: If you're 8 feet away from a door and with each move you advance half the distance to the door. How many moves will it take to reach the door?
rdl_0021.answer: Infinity! Technically you will never reach the door, as you can only move half the distance, no matter how small.

rdl_0022.question: There is an ancient invention, still used in some parts of the world today, that allows people to see through walls. What is it?

rdl_0023.question: Tom and his younger sister were fighting. Their mother was tired of the fighting and decided to punish them by making them stand on the same piece of newspaper in such a way that they couldn't touch each other. How did she accomplish this?
rdl_0023.answer: Tom's mother slid a newspaper under a door, each sibling standing on each side.

rdl_0024.question: I am a rock group that has 4 members, all of whom are dead, one of which was assasinated. What am I?
rdl_0024.answer: Mount Rushmore. Get it, rock group?

rdl_0025.question: The answer I give is yes, but what I mean is no. What was the question?

rdl_0026.question: I have a heart that never beats, I have a home but I never sleep. I can take a man's house and build another, And I love to play games with my many brothers. I am a king among fools. Who am I ?
rdl_0026.answer: The King of Hearts in a deck of cards.

rdl_0027.question: With pointed fangs it sits in wait, With piercing force it doles out fate, Over bloodless victims proclaiming its might, Eternally joining in a single bite. What is it?

rdl_0028.question: What is red and blue, and purple and green, No one can reach it, not even a Queen?

rdl_0029.question: Four cars come to a four-way stop, all coming from a different direction. They can't decide who got there first, so they all go forward at the same time. They do not crash into each other, but all four cars go. How is this possible?

rdl_0030.question: Where do Turkeys go to dance?

rdl_0031.question: I cover what's real, hide what is true, but sometimes bring out the courage in you. What am I?

rdl_0032.question: Why is a man in debt like a misty morning?
rdl_0032.answer: Because he is surrounded with dues (dews).

rdl_0033.question: I have a big mouth and I am also quite loud! I am NOT a gossip but I do get involved with everyone's dirty business. What am I?

rdl_0034.question: Who makes it, has no need of it. Who buys it, has no use for it. Those who use it can neither see nor feel it. What is it?

rdl_0035.question: What goes through the door without pinching itself, sits on the stove without burning itself, sits on the table, and is not ashamed?

rdl_0036.question: What work is it that the faster you work, the longer it is before you're done, and the slower you work, the sooner you're finished?

rdl_0037.question: I give you a group of three. One is sitting down, and will never get up. The second eats as much as is given to him, yet is always hungry. The third goes away and never returns. What are the three things?

rdl_0038.question: I know a word of letters three. Add two, and fewer there will be. What is it?

rdl_0039.question: Five hundred begins it, five hundred ends it, five in the middle is seen; first of all figures, the first of all letters, take up their stations between. Join all together, and then you will bring before you the name of an eminent king. Who is it?

rdl_0040.question: I build up castles. I tear down mountains. I make some men blind, I help others to see. What am I?

rdl_0041.question: Lovely and round, I shine with pale light, grown in the darkness, A lady's delight. What am I?

rdl_0042.question: At the sound of me, men may dream, Or stamp their feet. At the sound of me, women may laugh , Or sometimes weep. What am I?

rdl_0043.question: You can see nothing else When you look in my face, I will look you in the eye and I will never lie. What am I?

rdl_0044.question: You heard me before, Yet you hear me again, Then I die, 'Till you call me again. What am I?

rdl_0045.question: My life can be measured in hours, I serve by being devoured. Thin, I am quick. Fat, I am slow. Wind is my foe. What am I ?

rdl_0046.question: Weight in my belly, Trees on my back. Nails in my ribs, Feet I do lack. What am I?

rdl_0047.question: Three lives have I. Gentle enough to soothe the skin, Light enough to caress the sky, Hard enough to crack rocks. What am I?

rdl_0048.question: Lighter than what I am made of, more of me is hidden than is seen. What am I?

rdl_0049.question: If a man carried my burden he would break his back. I am not rich, but leave silver in my track. What am I?

rdl_0050.question: I am only useful when I am full, yet I am always full of holes. What am I?

rdl_0051.question: I am always hungry, I must always be fed, The finger I touch will soon turn red. What am I?

rdl_0052.question: I'm not really more than holes tied to more holes; I'm strong as good steel, though not as stiff as a pole. What am I?

rdl_0053.question: Whoever makes it, tells it not. Whoever takes it, knows it not. And whoever knows it wants it not. What is it?

rdl_0054.question: What gets wetter the more it dries?

rdl_0055.question: What kind of running means walking?

rdl_0056.question: Two words, my answer is only two words . To keep me, you must give me. What am I?

rdl_0057.question: What goes up when the rain comes down?

rdl_0058.question: Walk on the living, they don't even mumble. Walk on the dead, they mutter and grumble. What are they?

rdl_0060.question: What word contains all of the twenty six letters?

rdl_0061.question: There was a man who was born before his father, killed his mother , and married his sister. Yet, there was nothing wrong with what he had done. Why?
rdl_0061.answer: His father was in front of him when he was born, therefore he was born before him. His mother died while giving birth to him. Finally, he grew up to be a minister and married his sister at her ceremony.

rdl_0062.question: What 4-letter word can be written forward, backward or upside down, and can still be read from left to right?

rdl_0063.question: A large truck is crossing a bridge 1 mile long. The bridge can only hold 14000 lbs, which is the exact weight of the truck. The truck makes it half way across the bridge and stops. A bird lands on the truck. Does the bridge collapse?
rdl_0063.answer: No, it does not collapse. Because it has driven a half mile - you would subtract the gas used from the total weight of the truck.

rdl_0064.question: I'm sometimes white, Although sometimes I'm black. I take you there, But never bring you back. What am I?

rdl_0065.question: You are in a room that is completely bricked in on all four sides, including the ceiling and floor. You have nothing but a mirror and a wooden table in the room with you. How do you get out?
rdl_0065.answer: You look in the mirror you see what you saw, you take the saw and you cut the table in half, two halves make a whole, and you climb out the hole.

rdl_0066.question: The rungs of a 10-foot ladder attached to a ship are 1 foot apart. If the water is rising at the rate of one foot an hour, how long will it take until the water covers the ladder?
rdl_0066.answer: It will never cover the ladder because as the water rises, so will the floating ship.

rdl_0067.question: A sign on the barber's door says "I shave only those who do not shave themselves". Does the barber shave himself?
rdl_0067.answer: There is no answer; it's a paradox. It cannot be made to work.

rdl_0068.question: Two girls have the same parents and were born at the same hour on the same day of the same month, but they are not twins. How can this be possible?
rdl_0068.answer: They were not born in the same year.

rdl_0069.question: A pregnant lady named her children : Dominique, Regis, Michelle, Fawn, Sophie, and Lara. What will she name her next child? Jessica, Katie, Abby, or Tilly?
rdl_0069.answer: Tilly. She seems to follow the scale Do, Re, Me, Fa, So, La, and then Ti.

rdl_0070.question: A pet shop owner had a parrot with a sign on its cage that said "Parrot repeats everything it hears." A young man bought the parrot and for two weeks he spoke to it and it didn't say a word. He returned the parrot but the shopkeeper said he never lied about the parrot. How can this be?

rdl_0071.question: A woman was horrified to find a fly in her tea. The waiter took her cup and went into the kitchen and returned with a fresh cup of tea. She shouted, "You brought me the same tea!" How did she know?
rdl_0071.answer: She had already put sugar in it and when she tasted the new tea it was already sweet.

rdl_0072.question: Which word in the English language becomes shorter when it is lengthened?

rdl_0073.question: If you have three oranges and you take away two, how many will you have?

rdl_0074.question: What's the least number of chairs you would need around a table to sit four fathers, two grandfathers, and four sons?
rdl_0074.answer: Four. The trick is that the roles overlap. You only need four chairs because the same four people can simultaneously satisfy “four fathers,” “two grandfathers,” and “four sons.” A classic arrangement is: great‑grandfather, grandfather, father, and son. In this setup: The great‑grandfather and the grandfather are both grandfathers. All four can be fathers (the son can have a child not present). All four are also sons of someone. So the least number of chairs is four

rdl_0075.question: Look at me. I can bring a smile to your face, A tear to your eye, Or even a thought to your mind. But, I can't be seen. What am I?

rdl_0076.question: You do not want to have it, But when you do have it, You do not want to lose it. What is it?

rdl_0077.question: My first is often at the front door. My second is found in the cereal family. My third is what most people want. My whole is one of the United States. What am I?
rdl_0077.answer: MATRIMONY (mat rye money). Which is certainly a "united state"!

rdl_0078.question: What is more useful when it is broken?

rdl_0079.question: There is a frog, dead in the middle of an island. If he swims north, the distance to the mainland is 2 meters. If he swims south, the distance to the mainland is 3 meters. If he swims east or west, the distance is 4 meters. Which way does he swim?
rdl_0079.answer: He doesn't swim at all, he is dead.

rdl_0080.question: You live in a one story house made entirely of redwood. What color would the stairs be?
rdl_0080.answer: What stairs? You live in a one-story house.

rdl_0081.question: I can be created by humans, But they cannot control me. I suck on wood, paper and flesh alike. I can be more of a hindrance than help at times. To my creators, I seem to be everywhere at once. What am I?

rdl_0082.question: I am the fountain from which no one can drink. For many I am considered a necessary link. Like gold to all I am sought for, But my continued death brings wealth for all to want more. What am I?

rdl_0083.question: I fly in the air, But I am not always there. I cannot be touched, But I can be felt or held. Think very hard, But if you live near the equator, You may have a tough time seeing me. What am I?

rdl_0084.question: A man was shot to death while in his car. There were no powder marks on his clothing, which indicated that the gunman was outside the car. However, all the windows were up and the doors locked. After a close inspection was made, the only bullet holes discovered were on the man's body. How was he murdered?
rdl_0084.answer: The victim was in a convertible. He was shot when the top was down.
